### Front line
Ukrainian mapping project DeepState reported Russian forces occupied an additional 3.8 km² (all previously contested) and that 1.6 km² became newly contested, with Russian forces gaining 1% of Kostiantynivka. Another Ukrainian monitoring source, UkrDailyUpdate, reported 3.6 km² newly occupied and 1.1 km² newly contested, assessing that Russian forces occupied 2% of Kostiantynivka and that 6% of Dobropillia became contested. Across both datasets, there is verified agreement on 3.05 km² of newly occupied territory in Kostiantynivka. Concurrently, *The Economist* war-fire model detected 35 war-related satellite fires, located predominantly in Donetsk (16), Dnipropetrovsk (8), and Kharkiv (7) oblasts.

The Russian Ministry of Defence claimed its ground units breached and cleared the settlement of Serhiivka (Sergeevka) and captured Ukrainian soldiers in close-quarters fighting along the Dnipropetrovsk axis. The Russian military also claimed artillery and drone strikes on Ukrainian personnel shelters in Druzhkivka, equipment in the Orikhiv sector of Zaporizhia Oblast, and positions in Ozerne. These territorial advances and tactical claims remain unverified by independent sources.

### Strikes and losses
Open-source tracking platform GeoConfirmed documented several Russian attacks on civilian and infrastructure sites across Ukraine. A Russian Shahed drone struck a residential building in Vinnytsia, reportedly injuring six civilians and forcing 15 evacuations. GeoConfirmed also registered a Russian FPV drone strike on a minibus that reportedly killed one civilian and injured six, a separate Russian drone strike that reportedly killed three individuals, and an airstrike against a road dam. The Russian Ministry of Defence claimed its forces struck logistics terminals in Kharkiv, a cable-stayed bridge near Zaporizhzhia, and two commercial dry-cargo vessels allegedly carrying military supplies toward Chornomorsk and Odesa. A Russian tracking channel, lost_warinua, claimed the destruction of a Ukrainian ZiL-131 truck near Novoviktorovka, Donetsk Oblast.

Regarding Ukrainian strikes, GeoConfirmed verified that a Ukrainian drone attack on Belgorod, Russia, damaged the "MegaGRINN" shopping center, triggered a fire near a residential complex, and reportedly killed one person. GeoConfirmed also cataloged multiple reported Ukrainian Storm Shadow missile impacts that damaged and ignited buildings at the "Energiya" battery factory and the Proton factory. The Russian Ministry of Defence claimed its air defenses intercepted 532 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones overnight across numerous Russian regions and the Sea of Azov, alongside 38 additional drones downed during the day and two Ukrainian uncrewed surface vessels destroyed in the Black Sea.

### Official statements
The Russian Ministry of Defence issued a weekly summary claiming sustained advances and the capture of settlements in Zaporizhia Oblast, large-scale strikes against Ukrainian energy and transport facilities across 159 districts, an operational ceasefire on the Kherson front, and the repatriation of 270 Russian service members from captivity.

The Ukrainian Ministry of Defence announced the implementation of the "Tryzub" military surgery program. According to Ukrainian officials, the pilot initiative trains front-line surgical teams and anesthesiologists in combat trauma stabilization alongside international surgical associations from the United States and Europe.
